issues.issue: The attached agreement is between EMC and Morgan Stanley Mortgage Capital Inc., but the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement defines the "Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement" as one "between EMC and MSMCH" (Morgan Stanley Mortgage Capital Holdings LLC). The identity of the counterparty whose warranties were assigned is therefore contested on the face of the papers.

"Accepted Servicing Practices" is defined circularly by reference to "accepted mortgage servicing practices of prudent mortgage lending institutions," a standard with no fixed content. Whether particular servicing conduct complies cannot be answered from the words.

"Appraised Value" is simply the appraisal figure here, while the Loan-to-Value Ratio definition and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement's "Value" definition take the lesser of appraisal and purchase price. The valuation input for the LTV warranties depends on which of these controls.

The definition requires every Assignment of Mortgage to be "in recordable form and in blank," while Exhibit A-1(e) provides that if the assignment is to be recorded "the Mortgage shall be assigned to the Purchaser" and only otherwise delivered in blank. The two cannot both be satisfied for a recorded assignment.

The Closing Date is fixed as a single date, but Sections 9 and 10 repeatedly speak of "each Closing Date" and "the initial Closing Date," contemplating more than one. Whether further closings were possible turns on reconciling the definition with those sections.

The denominator is "the Appraised Value as determined pursuant to the Underwriting Guidelines," but "Underwriting Guidelines" is not a defined term in this Agreement and Appraised Value is separately defined without reference to any guidelines. The computation cannot be performed as written.
"Covered" is fixed only by Appendix E of Standard & Poor's Glossary, an undated external document that the parties do not reproduce. Which edition governs is not stated.
The definition reads "repurchased or to be repurchase or replaced," a plain grammatical error in the operative phrase identifying which loans are Deleted Mortgage Loans.

A payment is "Delinquent" here as soon as it is unpaid at the next Due Date, yet the loan-level warranties speak of payments "not yet 30 days Delinquent" and of being "30 days or more Delinquent." Stacking a day-count on this definition produces an ambiguous measure of delinquency.

The definition is truncated mid-sentence — "A Mortgage Loan secured by the pledge of stock allocated toa" — so what constitutes a Co-op Loan is not stated. Provisions that turn on Co-op Loan status have no complete definition to apply.

The Group 1 originator list (including Meritage and NC Capital) does not line up with the originators listed in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement's definition of MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans, although both purport to mark out the loans carrying seller-level warranties. Which loans carry which warranty set is not settled by either list alone.

The catch-all "or similar loan under any other applicable state, federal or local law" follows a list of specific statutory labels, leaving its reach to be settled by ejusdem generis. Whether a loan is "similar" to a "threshold" or "high risk home" loan is not answered by the text.

The Letter Agreement is between Morgan Stanley & Co. Incorporated and Bear, Stearns & Co. Inc. — neither of them a party to this Agreement — yet it fixes the Purchase Price Percentage on which Section 4 and the Repurchase Price depend. Whether its terms bind these parties is a real question.

The first sentence defines the Lifetime Rate Cap as a "provision" of the Mortgage Note, while the second states a substantive rate limit by reference to "the amount per annum set forth on the Mortgage Loan Schedule." The defined term therefore denotes both a clause and a number.

The denominator is "the lesser of (a) the Appraised Value ... and (b) if the Mortgage Loan was made to finance the acquisition ..., the purchase price," but for a refinancing there is no item (b), so the "lesser of" formula has only one term. How the ratio is computed for non-purchase loans is not stated.

The definition limits a Mortgage to an instrument "which creates a first lien on the Mortgaged Property," yet the Agreement expressly covers Second Lien Loans, defined as loans "secured by a second lien Mortgage," and the Exhibit F warranties address second liens throughout. On its own terms a second-lien loan has no qualifying Mortgage.

This definition limits the Exhibit A-2 items to those "in the possession of the applicable Servicer," while Exhibit A-2 itself limits them to items "in the possession of the applicable Seller." The two possession qualifiers cannot both be right.

"Mortgage Interest Rate Cap" and "Periodic Rate Cap" are separately defined to describe the same per-adjustment limit in the Mortgage Note, and the Qualified Substitute Mortgage Loan test uses only the former. Which definition governs a substitution test is not settled.

Mortgaged Property here extends to leasehold estates and co-op stock, while the companion "Mortgage" definition requires an instrument creating a first lien on that property and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement's "Mortgage" definition requires an estate in fee simple. The classes of eligible collateral do not line up.

The sentence "the absolute maximum amount by which the Mortgage Interest Rate there may increase or decrease" contains a stray word and is ungrammatical, and the definition then equates the Cap with "the rate set forth as such on the Mortgage Loan Schedule." The term denotes both a note provision and a schedule figure.

The whole price term is fixed by the Letter Agreement, a document between Morgan Stanley & Co. Incorporated and Bear, Stearns & Co. Inc. rather than the parties to this Agreement, and it also drives the Repurchase Price. Whether that outside document supplies an enforceable price here is genuinely open.

A Qualified Appraiser must be "duly appointed by the Seller," but the Mortgage Loans were originated by third-party Originators and merely purchased by the Seller, so no appraiser on those loans was appointed by the Seller. The appraisal warranty in Exhibit F cannot be satisfied on a literal reading.
"Qualified Correspondent" is elaborately defined but the term is used nowhere in the operative provisions or exhibits of this Agreement, leaving the definition without effect.
The definition ends "or their respective successors designated by the Purchasers," using a plural where the Agreement has a single Purchaser. It is unclear whose designation is required.

Component (b) reads "the accrued interest on such Stated Principal Balance at the Mortgage Interest Rate from the last interest paid to date through which interest has been paid ... through the date prior to the date of repurchase," a doubled and garbled formula for the interest period. The amount payable on repurchase cannot be computed with confidence from the words.

The closing words "none of which is a mobile home" trail a six-item list, so it is unclear whether the exclusion qualifies only Manufactured Homes or every category. The boundary between a Manufactured Home and a mobile home is also left unstated.

The Servicer is to be identified on Exhibit B, but Section 7 directs the reader to "the Mortgage Loan Schedule attached as Exhibit C" for the same information, and Exhibit C is the schedule of Prior Purchase and Servicing Agreements. The source of the servicer designation is inconsistently stated.

Servicing Rights are excluded from the conveyance by Subsection 6.01 and include Escrow Payments, late fees and amounts collected by the Seller, yet Subsection 6.02 vests in the Purchaser "all rights arising out of the Mortgage Loans including ... all funds received by the Seller ... after the Cut-off Date." The two provisions allocate the same collections to different parties.
